findings.title: Constructor validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
findings.body: The AccessTokenContext constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") on line 73, so rawTokenId is never null-checked. If a null raw token ID is supplied, the object is created and encodeTokenId can produce an ID ending in ':null' or later code can fail in an uncontrolled way. The check should be Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed").

findings.title: Token ID event matcher uses wrong substring and inverted check
findings.body: AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId checks items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut) and returns false when it is equal. The grant shortcut is the last two characters of the six-character prefix, so the code should use substring(4, 6), and the condition should reject when the value is not equal. As written, for a correct ID such as 'onrtac:...' with expected grant shortcut 'ac', substring(3, 5) is 'ta', so the matcher passes without verifying the grant type. This means the event tests do not actually validate the encoded grant shortcut and can hide regressions.

findings.title: Grant shortcuts are accepted without null or length validation
findings.body: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit stores OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() directly without checking that it is non-null and exactly two characters long. The default encoder/decoder hard-codes a six-character context prefix composed of three two-character shortcuts. A null shortcut will cause a NullPointerException when inserted into ConcurrentHashMap, and a one- or three-character shortcut will produce token IDs whose prefix cannot be parsed by getTokenContextFromTokenId, which expects length 6. Shortcut format should be validated when factories are registered.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut method breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
findings.body: Adding String getShortcut() to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory without a default implementation is a source and binary compatibility break for custom grant type factories compiled against earlier Keycloak versions. Existing implementations will fail to compile or can fail at runtime when the token-context encoder invokes the missing method. If this SPI is expected to be implemented by extensions, a default method or explicit migration contract is needed.

findings.title: Copy constructor removed from OAuth2GrantType.Context
findings.body: The change removes the public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context). If custom grant implementations or downstream code used this constructor, they will break at compile time or runtime with NoSuchMethodError. The addition of the grantType field could have preserved the copy constructor, or the removal should be explicitly documented as an incompatible SPI change.

findings.title: Dynamic grant shortcut refresh is non-atomic and does not enforce uniqueness
findings.body: getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut lazily add mappings for newly deployed grant types by writing to two separate ConcurrentHashMap instances without synchronization or duplicate-shortcut validation. If a newly deployed grant uses a shortcut already used by another grant, it can overwrite the existing shortcut-to-grant mapping, causing previously issued token IDs to decode to the wrong grant type. Concurrent updates can also observe partially updated state between the two maps. The maps should be updated atomically and uniqueness should be rechecked before insertion.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType succeeds due to NullPointerException from uninitialized sessionFactory
findings.body: The test creates DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory without calling postInit, so sessionFactory is null. When getTokenContextFromTokenId sees the unknown shortcut 'ac', it attempts to refresh grant mappings and throws NullPointerException, which is caught as RuntimeException. The test therefore does not verify the intended invalid-grant-shortcut behavior; it should initialize or mock the factory and assert the specific IllegalArgumentException.

findings.title: setFormParams does not update cached grantType
findings.body: OAuth2GrantType.Context.grantType is derived from formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE) only in the constructor. setFormParams replaces the form parameters but leaves grantType unchanged, so getGrantType() can return a stale value if the form parameters are modified after construction. The setter should update grantType or getGrantType should compute it from the current formParams.

findings.title: Javadoc says 3-letter shortcut but token encoding requires 2 characters
findings.body: The Javadoc for OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut says the shortcut is usually a 3-letter shortcut, but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider requires every grant shortcut to be exactly two characters to build the fixed six-character token ID prefix. Following the documented guidance would produce token IDs that cannot be decoded by the default provider. The documentation should state the required two-character format.
